diagnostics.message: kubectl_manifest.karpenter_provisioner defines a Provisioner whose spec sets `providerRef: { name: default }`, i.e. it references the AWSNodeTemplate named "default" that is created by kubectl_manifest.karpenter_node_template. The graph only records a dependency on module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (needed for the Karpenter CRDs), so Terraform is free to apply the Provisioner before the AWSNodeTemplate exists. Karpenter then cannot resolve its provider (`default`), the Provisioner never becomes usable and nodes are never provisioned. It must be ordered after kubectl_manifest.karpenter_node_template (e.g. `depends_on = [kubectl_manifest.karpenter_node_template]`).

When the self-managed CoreDNS chart replaces the EKS default deployment, resource null_resource.modify_kube_dns annotates and labels the already existing `kube-dns` Service (meta.helm.sh/release-name, meta.helm.sh/release-namespace, app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm) so that Helm is allowed to adopt it. The self-managed CoreDNS helm_release.addon only depends on null_resource.remove_default_coredns_deployment (via its `blueprints.connection` set value); it has no ordering edge to null_resource.modify_kube_dns. Terraform can therefore run the Helm install in parallel with the annotation step, and Helm fails with "Service \"kube-dns\" ... exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata". The helm release must depend on null_resource.modify_kube_dns.
